pharm: Selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist; human metabolite of hydroxyzine
quick: Ask a health professional before use
summary: Cetirizine is a second-generation H1-antihistamine for temporary relief of allergic rhinitis and upper-respiratory allergy symptoms. It is less sedating than first-generation agents but drowsiness may still occur. Dose adjustment is advised in renal or hepatic impairment.
indications: Temporary relief of symptoms due to hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies: runny nose, sneezing, itchy/watery eyes, itching of the nose or throat

dosage.c: Adults and children 6 years and over
dosage.d: 5 mg or 10 mg once daily depending on symptom severity
dosage.n: Do not take more than 10 mg in 24 hours
Do not take more than 5 mg in 24 hours

dosage.d: 2.5 mg once daily; may increase to max 5 mg once daily or 2.5 mg every 12 hours
dosage.n: Do not give more than 5 mg in 24 hours
Ask a doctor; a different (lower) dose may be needed

admin: May be taken with or without water
Chewable tablets must be chewed or crushed completely before swallowing
Take once daily, typically same time each day
moa: Selective antagonist of peripheral histamine H1 receptors, blocking histamine-mediated allergic responses (vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, pruritus). It penetrates the CNS poorly, accounting for reduced sedation versus first-generation antihistamines.

absolute: Prior allergic reaction to cetirizine or any product ingredient
Hypersensitivity to an antihistamine containing hydroxyzine
monitor: Concurrent tranquilizers or sedatives - ask a doctor or pharmacist before use

preg: If pregnant, ask a health professional before use.
lact: If breast-feeding, use is not recommended.
renal: In kidney disease, ask a doctor before use; a different (reduced) dose may be required.
hepatic: In liver disease, ask a doctor before use; a different (reduced) dose may be required.

interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcoholic drinks; alcohol, sedatives, and tranquilizers may increase drowsiness.

emergency: Signs of allergic reaction (seek medical help right away)

monitoring: Watch for drowsiness/sedation, especially when driving or operating machinery
Reassess if an allergic reaction to the product occurs
counsel: Drowsiness may occur; be careful when driving a motor vehicle or operating machinery
Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking this product
Stop use and ask a doctor if an allergic reaction occurs and seek medical help right away
Ask a doctor before use if you have liver or kidney disease
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if taking tranquilizers or sedatives
Keep out of reach of children; in case of overdose, contact a Poison Control Center (1-800-222-1222)
pearls: Cetirizine is the active human metabolite of hydroxyzine; avoid in patients with hydroxyzine hypersensitivity
Less sedating than first-generation antihistamines, but drowsiness is more common than with fexofenadine or loratadine
Lower dose for elderly (5 mg/day) and in renal or hepatic impairment
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose.
overdose: In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away (1-800-222-1222).
